2026-08-31T12:39:18.9338158Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9338909Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9339240Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9339724Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9340135Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9340630Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9342192Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9344746Z >
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9347094Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9349905Z >
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9350700Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9351470Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9351654Z ### How to Use
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9352199Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9352927Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9353891Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9354075Z ```bash
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9354628Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9355747Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9356410Z ```
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9356622Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9356908Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9357445Z ```bash
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9357990Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9358776Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9359989Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9360761Z ```
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9361049Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9361696Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9362570Z ```bash
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9363324Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9364372Z ```
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9364589Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9364928Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9365695Z ```bash
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9366229Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9367093Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9367793Z ```
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9368000Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9368257Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9369042Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9370477Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9372086Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9372264Z ```bash
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9372712Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9374061Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9374914Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9375234Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9375725Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9376739Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9377549Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9378023Z ```
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9378231Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9378967Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9380229Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9380404Z ```bash
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9381086Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9381966Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9382675Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9383110Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9383679Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9384487Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9385044Z ```
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9385243Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9385454Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9386654Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9387640Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9388620Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9389714Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9391146Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9391705Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9391886Z ### Notes
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9392099Z 
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9392712Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9394326Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9395937Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9397190Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9398407Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9399529Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9400829Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-31T12:39:18.9401535Z </mcp-clis>
